title: Internal testimony of the Spirit — efficient cause, not a heard medium
source_text: XXVI. Et omnes quidem Theologi, tam nostri, quam Romanenses, ad hoc, ut aliquis Dei verbum & revelationem, sicuti par est, suscipiat, & de ea certus reddatur, agnoscunt opus esse arcana quadam Spiritus Sancti operatione, quam communiter vocant internum Spiritus sancti testimonium. Sed nemo eorum, quod sciam, per testimonium istud intelligit expressam aliquam Dei vocem, quam fidelis intus audiat, & sentiat, & cujus authoritate, sic velut indicio, propositam extrinsecus revelationem amplectatur. Sed per hoc in genere non aliud intelligunt, quam operationem quandam Spiritus Sancti, qua fidem nobis ingenerat, & quae se ad fidem non habet instar medii, sive argumenti, quo fides innitatur, sed potius instar causae efficientis. Nec etiam, ex eorum communi sententia, interna illa Spiritus Sancti operatio necessitatem excludit aliquorum mediorum & incitamentorum, quorum intuitu mens nostra ad suscipiendam revelationem, quae ipsi proponitur, moveatur atque impellatur.
pass_a_gloss: And indeed all Theologians, both ours and the Roman, for this — that someone receive God’s word and revelation as is fitting, and be made certain of it — acknowledge that there is need of a certain secret operation of the Holy Spirit, which they commonly call the internal testimony of the Holy Spirit. But none of them, so far as I know, understands by that testimony some express voice of God which the faithful hears and feels within, and by whose authority, as by a sort of indication, he embraces the revelation proposed from without. But by this in general they understand nothing other than a certain operation of the Holy Spirit by which He generates faith in us, and which stands to faith not after the manner of a medium or argument on which faith rests, but rather after the manner of an efficient cause. Nor even, on their common opinion, does that internal operation of the Holy Spirit exclude the necessity of some means and incentives by whose regard our mind is moved and driven to receive the revelation proposed to it.
pass_b_english: Reformed and Roman: need Spirit’s secret operation — ‘internal testimony’.
Not an audible inner voice used as medium/argument.
Efficient cause of faith; still uses means/incentives that move the mind.
